content: The Salamander Trust, with support from the Athena Network and commissioned by the World Health Organization (WHO), convened a Global Reference Group (GRG) composed of women living with HIV from diverse backgrounds. This group conducted the largest global survey to date on the values and preferences of women living with HIV regarding their sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR) priorities. The findings of this survey were presented at a WHO stakeholder consultation on SRHR for women living with HIV, where their implications were discussed. This consultation led to the development of a human rights framework that informed the creation of a new WHO guideline on SRHR for women living with HIV. On the International Day of Action for Women’s Health, the Eurasian Women’s Network on AIDS released a community-friendly Russian translation of the WHO Consolidated SRHR Guidelines for women living with HIV. The findings of the Global Values and Preferences Survey (GVPS) were also presented at the International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics (FIGO) conference in Vancouver. Two articles based on the GVPS findings, focusing on gender-based violence (GBV) and mental health, were published in the Journal of the International AIDS Society (JIAS) Special Supplement and made available in Spanish. Additionally, an article summarizing key findings appeared in Open Democracy. In Ukraine, the national network of women living with HIV adapted the GVPS findings and launched a 1,000-respondent survey to further investigate the SRHR status of women living with HIV in the country, supported by UN Women’s Istanbul office. Regional WHO webinars were held to launch the guideline in various regions, including WPRO/SEARO, PAHO (in Spanish and English), and the African Region (in English). Positive Women presented their shadow report based on SRHR research findings at the 66th Session of the Committee on the Elimination of Discrimination Against Women (CEDAW) in Geneva. The WHO Consolidated Guideline on SRHR for women living with HIV was officially released, and the Salamander Trust, in collaboration with networks of women living with HIV and allies, launched the Women Engage. initiative. This included a guide on the involvement of women living with HIV in the prevention, screening, early diagnosis, treatment, and research of cervical cancer. The guideline emphasized the ethical, strategic, and meaningful involvement of women living with HIV from the outset of policy and program development. In Kenya, the Women Fighting AIDS in Kenya (WOFAK) organization, established in 1994 by women living with HIV, has been instrumental in reducing HIV-related stigma and empowering women. WOFAK’s work has focused on inspiring self-respect, emotional strength, and coping skills among women living with HIV. The organization has also worked to involve men and opinion leaders in recognizing the value of women living with HIV as equal citizens. Despite progress, HIV-related prejudice resurfaces at critical points in women’s lives, such as when seeking support for conception, counseling on sexual health, or confidential and rights-sensitive services. These challenges are compounded by violence, stigma, and discrimination, particularly for women expressing diverse gender identities or sexual orientations. WOFAK has been advocating for the full implementation of the 2017 WHO SRHR Guideline in Kenya, recognizing it as a win-win for both women and service providers. The organization piloted the Salamander Trust’s Generic Checklist of Actions to assess gaps in existing SRHR services and policies. This process empowered women living with HIV to advocate for their rights and engage with policymakers. Workshops were held in counties with high maternal, newborn, and adolescent health needs, such as Lamu, Isiolo, and Migori. Women activists from these counties led advocacy efforts, tailoring their approaches to local challenges, including cultural and religious sensitivities. Healthcare providers in these counties expressed gratitude for the information provided through the workshops, which equipped them to better implement the guideline’s recommendations. WOFAK also shared the guideline with county networks of women living with HIV, many of whom requested translations into Swahili and other local languages. The Transgender Law Center (TLC), the largest national trans-led organization in the United States, has been advocating for the self-determination of transgender and gender non-conforming individuals. In 2015, TLC launched the Positively Trans project to empower transgender people living with HIV through advocacy and self-representation. The project, guided by a National Advisory Board of individuals living with HIV, has prioritized addressing the double stigma faced by transgender individuals due to their gender identity and HIV status. Positively Trans has conducted research on violence and discrimination experienced by transgender people living with HIV, highlighting the need for gender-affirming care and mental health support. The findings from these efforts underscore the importance of addressing the unique needs of transgender individuals, including access to safe and respectful sexual and reproductive health services. The project has also emphasized the value of community-led research and advocacy, ensuring that findings are shared with the communities involved before being disseminated more broadly. This approach has strengthened the relationship between researchers, funders, and communities, fostering mutual understanding and collaboration. In recent years, there has been increased funding and interest in research exploring the health of under-researched communities, such as transgender individuals. The International Transgender Fund, established with an initial pool of $20 million, has focused on supporting trans-led organizations globally, particularly in developing countries. These efforts aim to address intersectional issues driving HIV epidemics and promote equity in funding distribution. The hope is that these initiatives will serve as a tipping point for advancing transgender rights and reproductive justice on a global scale.
